key_insight: A SCAPS-1D plus machine-learning workflow can efficiently rank multilayer perovskite solar-cell stacks and identify high-efficiency, lead-free designs with strong explanatory insight.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical optimization framework for selecting ETL, absorber, and HTL combinations that can reduce trial-and-error in perovskite device engineering.
method: Trained an ML model on a representative subset to predict PCE for unexplored stacks.
Used SHAP to identify the most influential descriptors and verify top candidates with full device simulations.
evidence_signal: Leave-One-Group-Out cross-validation showed reliable ranking performance, and the top predicted structures were confirmed by SCAPS-1D, including FTO/TiO2/Cs2AgBiBr6/NiO/Ag at 28.85% PCE.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality and representativeness of the simulated training subset, so predictions may be less reliable for material combinations outside the sampled design space.
paper_title: Multilayer Screening of Double and Conventional Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D and Machine Learning: Optimization of ETL, HTL, and Absorber for High-Efficiency Architectures
